title: Load balancing: round robin, least connections and session persistence

videos.script: A website has one name, and behind it there are three servers. {{one-name}} Something has to decide which server answers each request. That something is a load balancer. {{choose}} In this lesson you watch it decide, one request at a time. Each server answers with its own name, so every choice is printed. {{rr}} First, round robin. The servers take turns, and weights give a bigger server more turns. {{slow}} Then a slow download arrives. Round robin keeps sending work to the busy server anyway. Least connections notices it, and sends the next requests elsewhere. {{hash}} Then you pin each client to one server, by hashing its address. Four clients out of five land on the same server, and you will see why. {{cookie}} The better way is a cookie. The balancer adds one to the first reply, and brings the visitor back to the same server every time. {{dies}} Until that server dies. Without health checks, the pinned visitor gets an error, while everybody else is fine. {{redispatch}} With checks, the visitor is moved. What was in the dead server's memory is gone either way. That is where the lesson ends.
